title: Foundations
intro: The language of events and the handful of rules every probability calculation rests on: the axioms, counting, conditioning, independence and Bayes' theorem.

blocks.text: Before random variables and distributions there are events, and three questions about them: how likely is an event, how does learning one event change the likelihood of another, and when does it not change it at all. Everything later reduces to these.

items: Sample Spaces and Events (#/probability/foundations/sample-spaces-and-events): outcomes, events as sets, and the probability of a union.
The Axioms of Probability (#/probability/foundations/axioms): Kolmogorov's three axioms and the rules that follow, including inclusion–exclusion and continuity.
Counting (#/probability/foundations/counting): permutations, combinations, multinomials, stars and bars, and the birthday problem.
Conditional Probability (#/probability/foundations/conditional-probability): conditioning, the multiplication rule and the law of total probability.
Independence (#/probability/foundations/independence): independent events, pairwise versus mutual independence, and conditional independence.
Bayes' Theorem (#/probability/foundations/bayes-theorem): inverting conditional probabilities, base rates, and the odds form.
J. K. Blitzstein and J. Hwang, Introduction to Probability, 2nd edition, CRC Press (2019), chapters 1 and 2
S. M. Ross, A First Course in Probability, 10th edition, Pearson (2019), chapters 1 to 3
